minutes.headline: Assessors agreed to research five years of abatement history before recommending the overlay; only executive minutes were voted.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the interim principal assessor's status report, reviewed prior minutes, and debated the FY2025 overlay recommendation, deciding a member would research five years of abatement and exemption history before the next Monday meeting. They also discussed new growth, the annual town report draft, the five-year revaluation status, senior/blind/veteran exemption amounts, and the website and mission statement. The only recorded vote approved the executive session minutes of January 22 as amended.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the executive session of January 22 as amended

budget_items.what_was_said: The mapping vendor's neighborhood map cost an extra amount beyond the original service contract, which the town manager approved.

The overlay balance across all years was stated, and last year's overlay was funded through an increase at annual town meeting. Not all of it is spendable because abatements and exemptions are still coming.

The town manager suggested keeping the overlay at the amount used for several years. One member wanted a five-year trend analysis first; others noted past boards never used it up and the state has not pushed back.
Excess overlay can be released only at the request of the Select Board and a vote of the assessors; it cannot be used for schools.
The finance director chose a conservative new growth estimate below the assessor's own estimate; it was already voted earlier.
The state partially reimburses exemptions up to its recommended amounts and nothing above them; the reimbursement appears as a total, not by exemption.
Local senior and blind exemption amounts exceed the state recommendations while veterans are at the recommendation; doubling at town meeting was discussed with cost impact to be calculated.

budget_items.topic: Revenue estimates vs actuals in town report
budget_items.what_was_said: Actual receipts came in below estimates, for example motor vehicle excise, which is the basis for next year's budget.

decisions.decision: A board member will research five years of abatement and exemption history (Gateway tax certification) and return with an overlay recommendation at the next Monday meeting.
Next meeting date to be changed from January 22 to January 29; executive session items to be placed on the February 5 agenda.
The annual report will describe last year's abatement increase as roughly 30 times the norm rather than a percentage.
Exemption amount discussion tabled until the five-year numbers are gathered and a cost estimate can be made.
Wednesday meeting with the vendor will cover condos and lake properties; approval is not expected that night and the vendor may be asked back.
January 18 minutes considered already approved; January 8 minutes accepted with a name misspelling to be fixed; January 22 minutes held.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors did not settle the FY2025 overlay; a member will research five years of abatement and exemption history and report back at the next Monday meeting.
The town manager suggested keeping the overlay at the level used for several years, while one member asked for a five-year trend analysis first.
The board tabled any change to senior, blind and veteran exemption amounts until the five-year numbers are gathered and a cost estimate is made.
The board will describe last year's jump in abatements in the annual report as a multiple of the norm rather than a percentage.
The board accepted the January 8 minutes with a name correction and held the January 22 minutes; no roll-call votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: The overlay is the reserve for property tax abatements and exemptions, so the amount set for FY2025 affects how much the town has to raise through the tax levy.
Local senior and blind exemption amounts are above the state's recommended levels, so any change would be a town meeting vote with a cost to other taxpayers, and the cost estimate is not yet done.
